attrs.evidence: emission_conformance.mjs 9/9 over 9 fixtures. THE FIXTURE FAMILY WAS CORRECTED AT B6.1: what B6 called the I-4c witness is add(input x, input y) with {x:2,y:3}, and 2+3 == 3+2, so it is exactly the SYMMETRIC fixture INSTANTIATION_FALSIFIERS I-4c rejects as 'a test whose output cannot reveal the defect it is named for'. It is KEPT under an honest name -- 'two-port collapse' -- because what it actually proves is worth having: it closes to the SAME closed template as add(const 2, const 3), so two different source and instantiation histories become indistinguishable to emission. The ACTUAL I-4c, x + (x + y) with {x:2,y:3}, is added beside it: 7 under the correct binding and 8 under the swap, and a distinct closed template (ctmpl-efba3154...) already, so no fixture had to be invented to force distinctness. E-F1 now uses an unconstrained quotient-visible drift and covers 9/9; E-8 keeps the commutativity-dependent equivalence and covers the 6 add-bearing fixtures. AND THE PASS HEADLINE IS DERIVED FROM MEASURED FIELDS. B6's summary line stated that a semantics-preserving allocation change moves target_term_sem_id and is refused on all 8, and that an alpha-equivalent emitter differs in id on every fixture -- both FALSE, and both contradicted by the cases printed immediately above them in the same run. The cases had been corrected when the measurement arrived; the summary kept the pre-measurement theory, and the summary is what lands in RESULTS.txt. Every quantity the final line states is now a field written by the case that measured it. B6.2 ADDS THE DUAL FALSIFIER AND SPLITS THE DETERMINISM CLAIM. Changing ONLY CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE.label_counter_start from 0 to 7000, freshness and equality structure preserved: emitted BYTES differ on 7/9 fixtures, target_term_sem_id is IDENTICAL on 9/9, closed_template_sem_id is IDENTICAL on 9/9, CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_ID MOVES, and EMISSION_SEM_ID, TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID, TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING_SEM_ID, LOWERING_SEM_ID and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID all stand still. E-1 is split into E-1a SEMANTIC RELATION DETERMINISM (same closed template -> same target_term_sem_id, owned by EMISSION_SEM_ID) and E-1b CANONICAL BYTE REPRODUCIBILITY (same closed template + same profile -> same bytes, owned by CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_ID); E-2b asserts the profile is a distinct identity AND is interpreted, by measuring that the first dup label the emitter actually produces equals the start the profile declares. Emission 11/11 over 9 fixtures.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED by @4 at B6.3. @3 stated the semantic/serialization split and shipped a projection that was true of ONE field: CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE held one interpreted knob beside five English sentences and hashed all six, so the very defect @3 records -- an id bound to a DESCRIPTION of a policy rather than to the policy -- survived one field over and in both directions. Reword binder_spelling: profile id MOVED, bytes unchanged. Change the actual binder spelling {f0,f1} -> {q0,q1}: bytes differed on 6 of 9 fixtures, profile id STOOD STILL. And @3's own byte-reproducibility theorem was scoped one term short, naming the profile as its whole precondition when a profile is CONFIGURATION that an implementation may decline to read.
attrs.statement: THE CANONICAL EMITTER DETERMINISTICALLY REALISES ITS DECLARED RELATION, over a FAMILY of fixtures rather than the one witness it had. closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, and a conformance record is those three fields and no more: the relation's id is CONSTANT across every fixture, because a per-fixture emission id would identify invocations rather than the relation -- instantiation-identity@1's finding, one relation downstream. VERIFICATION IS BY RECONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY SELF-AGREEMENT: the verifier rebuilds the closed template from (program, inputs), re-emits through the canonical emitter, and canonicalises with an oracle IT WAS HANDED rather than one the emitter chose. An emitter that produced the artifact and certified its identity would verify a wrong emission against itself. EMISSION IS A FUNCTION OF THE CLOSED TEMPLATE AND NOT OF THE PROGRAM, which the family MEASURES rather than assumes: add(const 2, const 3) and add(input x, input y) closed with {x:2,y:3} are THE SAME CLOSED TEMPLATE and emit identically. Instantiation has already erased the difference between a literal and a port bound to that literal, and an emitter producing different bytes for those two would be reading something it is not entitled to see. The check is the implication in the direction that can be wrong -- equal domain implies equal codomain, different domain implies no collision -- rather than a blanket injectivity claim that would be false. THREE IDENTITIES FORM A LADDER, AND EMISSION PROVES THE MIDDLE ONE. exact emitted BYTES --quotient alpha-renaming and label SPELLING--> target_term_sem_id --execute, normalise, decode--> outcome_sem_id. Different bytes may share a target_term_sem_id; different target_term_sem_ids may share an outcome_sem_id; this battery demonstrates BOTH. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECEIPT IS EXACT: EmissionReceipt carries no byte digest, so it does not and MUST NOT claim 'these exact bytes were produced'. It proves that the closed template maps, under this emission semantics, to this canonical target-term identity. If byte reproducibility ever needs proving it belongs beside executable_artifact_id as PROVENANCE, not inside a semantic relation whose own codomain deliberately erases the spelling. B6 framed this as a PAIR -- canonical determinism against semantic equivalence -- which is right at the top and hides that target_term_sem_id sits BETWEEN bytes and meaning rather than at either end. AND THE TWO ADVERSARIES ARE DIFFERENT ANIMALS, which B6 fused. CANONICAL DRIFT (E-F1): same closed template, same relation id, a changed claim about the target term, therefore REFUSE -- it needs NO semantic equivalence and therefore applies to every fixture. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE (E-8): different target_term_sem_id, SAME meaning -- it requires a real equivalence and is applicable only where the fragment supplies one. Fused, the canonical-drift falsifier would lose its adversary the moment a non-commutative operator arrived, for a reason having nothing to do with what it proves. CANONICAL DETERMINISM: a structural change to the emitter moves target_term_sem_id and the receipt carrying it is REFUSED. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE: that same alternate emitter's output decodes to the same outcome. The first says the relation is a function; the second says target_term_sem_id identifies THIS emitter's output rather than the term's meaning. Collapsing them yields either 'reordering is a semantic change' or 'emission may drift as long as the answer matches', and the second is how a compiler stops being reproducible quietly. AND THE MUTATION THAT EXHIBITS THE PAIR HAD TO BE MEASURED. An ALPHA-EQUIVALENT alternate emitter produces the IDENTICAL target_term_sem_id on every fixture -- the canonical signature is byte-equivariant under alpha-renaming and label permutation by asserted law (L-BYTES-1) -- so renaming cannot witness this at all and the adversary must be STRUCTURAL. Reordering add's operands is meaning-preserving on THIS fragment because addition commutes, and would not be for a non-commutative operator; the caveat is part of the law rather than a footnote to it. NO NATIVE FILM IS REQUIRED OR USED. The transition relation carries its own evidence, and defining the emitter's correctness by what its output computes would put the runtime inside the compiler's contract -- the layer collapse lowering_spike.layer_separation exists to refuse. A downstream composition runs last and is LABELLED an integration theorem; every conformance case stands without it. AND THE PROJECTION NOW MATCHES THE ONTOLOGY, WHICH AT @2 IT DID NOT. B6.1 ruled label spelling nonsemantic in prose while EMISSION_SEM_ID went on hashing the allocation policy, and the resulting defect was INVERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE: editing the PROSE describing the counter moved EMISSION_SEM_ID while bytes and target terms were untouched, and editing the ACTUAL counter inside emit() changed the bytes on 7 of 9 fixtures while EMISSION_SEM_ID stood still. The id was bound to a DESCRIPTION of the policy rather than to the policy -- B1.1's finding that governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when reworded, recurring in the one field B6.1 had corrected the wording of without moving. THE SPLIT: the SEMANTIC target-term encoding commits to Church and add structure, to DUP label EQUALITY AND FRESHNESS relationships, to the alpha and label-permutation quotient, and to the semantic refusals. The CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE commits to counter start, allocation traversal, binder spelling and exact representative bytes, under CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_ID, which NO semantic identity cites. THE PROFILE IS INTERPRETED AND NOT DESCRIBED: emit() reads label_counter_start from it, exactly as lower() reads op_lowering_rules since B2.1, so the policy cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving the profile id. An English sentence beside a hard-coded constant is two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed, which is precisely how the field came to be false in both directions. AND NO ALLOCATION POLICY IS HASHED UPSTREAM EITHER: TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING named a counter start, so changing an emitter's allocation re-cut the TEMPLATE, LOWERING and INSTANTIATION identities -- a layer whose whole claim is that no allocation exists in it cannot also commit to how one is performed two layers down. THE RECEIPT IS UNCHANGED AND STAYS THAT WAY: no byte digest is added. Exact bytes are PROVENANCE and belong beside executable_artifact_id.
